report:
### Conclusion
The health claim is **true**. The adjuvanted recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV, brand name Shingrix) significantly reduces the incidence of shingles (herpes zoster) in adults aged 70 years or older.

### Research Findings
* **Clinical Trial Data:** In the landmark randomized Phase III trial (ZOE-70), two doses of the recombinant zoster vaccine demonstrated roughly 90% to 91% efficacy in preventing shingles among adults aged 70 years or older. High protection was maintained across age sub-categories (70–79 years as well as 80+ years), while also significantly reducing the risk of postherpetic neuralgia.
* **Public Health Guidance:** The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) reports that Shingrix is 91% effective at preventing shingles in immunocompetent adults 70 years and older, recommending it as the preferred shingles vaccine.

### Sources
* CDC Shingles Vaccination Overview: https://www.cdc.gov/shingles/vaccines/index.html
* The New England Journal of Medicine (ZOE-70 Trial): https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1603800
* PubMed Summary: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27626517/
